Watts made this hymn from Psalm 73:22, 3, 6, 17–20, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

22I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You. 3For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. 6Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them. 17until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end. 18Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin. 19How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors! 20Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form. PSALM 73:22, 3, 6, 17–20 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 73
Lord, what a thoughtless wretch was I, To mourn, and murmur, and repine To see the wicked plac'd on high, In pride and robes of honour shine! STANZA I
